_README: THE CONTRACT BETWEEN THE VMS AND THE HEAD-COUNT SERVICE.
One camera row exactly as GET /api/internal/headcount/cameras emits it, and
exactly as ai/head-count/src/headcount/source.py reads it. Three tests read
this file and none of them can pass alone:
backend/test/headcountChain.test.js     the backend EMITS this shape
ai/head-count/tests/test_vms_contract.py the service PARSES this shape
frontend/.../zone-model.test.js          the editor BUILDS these zones
It exists because every bug found in this feature has been a boundary bug --
two correct components disagreeing -- and a unit test on either side of a
boundary cannot see the boundary. A camera ticked for counting and excluded
by the master AI switch; a zone saved to the registry and never applied by
the detector. Both were invisible to full-green test suites on both sides.
CHANGING THIS FILE IS CHANGING THE CONTRACT. If a field moves or is renamed,
all three tests fail, in all three languages, which is the entire point. Do
not edit it to make a test pass.
`zones[]` is what the zone editor produces (frontend cameraPayload) after the
backend's sanitiseZones has validated it: normalised 0..1 points, >= 3 of
them, so a shape drawn on a preview keeps its meaning at any resolution.
`threshold` is 0 BECAUSE there are two zones. A camera-level limit only has
a meaning when exactly one zone sits on exactly one camera -- then the zone
IS the camera and cameraPayload pushes its capacity here. With two rooms in
one view, "12 people on this camera" answers no question anybody asked, so
the capacity stays on each zone. Pinned here because a fixture carrying a
limit AND two zones would be a shape the product cannot produce.
WHAT WE PROMISE AN OPERATOR WHEN WE SWITCH A CAMERA'S AI ON FOR COUNTING.
This is here because the worst defect in this feature was a BROKEN PROMISE,
not a wrong value. The consent dialog said, in these words, that faces are
not matched -- while the repair button two inches away went through a route
that started face recognition and spent a face licence. Both call sites were
individually correct. Nothing tested that the promise and the code agreed,
because the promise was English in a React file and the code was a function
in a Node service.
So the promise is written down once, and both ends assert against it:
backend/test/headcountTurnsAiOn.js   masterOnForFeature HONOURS it
frontend .../counting-status.test.js the dialog SAYS it
Weaken the code and the backend test fails. Quietly drop the sentence from
the dialog and the frontend test fails. Change your mind about the promise
and you have to change it here, which makes both ends move together and
leaves a diff that says what was decided.
